drug_class: Monoclonal antibody / EGFR inhibitor (targeted cancer therapy)
purpose: Cetuximab is used to treat certain types of colorectal (colon and rectal) cancer and head and neck cancers. It is often used when cancer has spread or when other treatments have not worked well enough. Your doctor may use it alone or in combination with other cancer treatments like chemotherapy or radiation.
how_it_works: Your cancer cells have a protein on their surface called EGFR (think of it like a door handle that helps cancer cells grow). Cetuximab is a specially designed antibody that locks onto that door handle and blocks it, so the cancer cells cannot get the signal they need to grow and multiply. By blocking this signal, it helps slow down or stop the cancer from spreading.
common_side_effects: The most common side effect is a skin rash that looks like acne, often on the face, neck, and chest — this is actually a sign the medicine may be working. You may also experience dry, itchy, or cracked skin, nail changes, mouth sores, fatigue (feeling very tired), nausea, diarrhea, and low magnesium levels in your blood. Infusion reactions (feeling flushed, short of breath, or having chills during or after the IV drip) can also happen.
warnings: Serious allergic or infusion reactions can occur, especially during the first treatment — you will be closely monitored. Cetuximab can cause a dangerous drop in magnesium and other electrolytes, so your blood will be checked regularly. It can also worsen lung problems (interstitial lung disease), so tell your doctor right away if you feel short of breath. Avoid prolonged sun exposure as your skin will be more sensitive. This medicine is not recommended during pregnancy or breastfeeding — talk to your doctor about contraception.
typical_dosing: Cetuximab is given as an intravenous (IV) infusion — meaning it goes directly into your vein through a drip at a clinic or hospital. The typical starting dose is 400 mg per square meter of your body surface area given over about 2 hours, followed by weekly doses of 250 mg per square meter given over about 1 hour. Your doctor will determine the exact schedule based on your treatment plan.
